title: API Token Controls
scope: Admin controls, logging and revocation for API credentials on SaaS platforms. Sourced from vendor documentation; not an audit of any tenant.

definitions.conditional: Documented, with plan, policy or endpoint conditions.
definitions.excluded: The named control explicitly does not cover this credential.
definitions.not_supported: Vendor documentation states this credential lacks the control.
definitions.unknown: No source found either way. Not a negative finding.
definitions.not_verified: No source found either way. Not a negative finding.
definitions.not_applicable: Does not apply to this credential.
definitions.limited: Documented for a narrower case only.

providers.name: Atlassian Jira / Confluence Cloud
providers.scope_notes: Product IP allowlisting requires Premium/Enterprise. SAML SSO typically requires Atlassian Guard Standard or an included entitlement.

controls.name: IP allowlists
controls.what: Users outside allowed IPs/locations cannot reach Jira/Confluence content, including via the APIs.
controls.setting: admin.atlassian.com > Security > Device security > IP allowlists
controls.plan: Premium (Jira, JSM, Confluence, Compass) or Enterprise (Analytics, Focus)
controls.quote: Users also won't be able to access that app programmatically via the APIs.

controls.name: Block user apps (user-installed apps)
controls.what: Restricts app installation to admins so end users cannot grant third-party (3LO) apps access.
controls.setting: Atlassian Administration > Apps > [site] > Connected apps > settings > Block user apps
controls.quote: Organization and Site admins can also choose to restrict app installation to admin level by selecting Block user apps in the Connected apps settings.

controls.name: Uninstall connected app
controls.what: Uninstalling a 3LO app from the site revokes all users' grants.
controls.setting: Atlassian Administration > Apps > [site] > Connected apps > Manage authorization > Uninstall
controls.quote: For OAuth 2.0 (3LO) apps such as “Atlassian for VS Code” , the Uninstall button revokes all users.

controls.name: Marketplace and custom app access control (data security policy)
controls.what: Blocks eligible installed apps from user-generated content, org-wide or in selected spaces; finer allow-lists need Guard.
controls.setting: Atlassian Administration > Security > Data protection > Data security policy > Marketplace and custom app access
controls.plan: Any plan to block all; Atlassian Guard Standard/Premium for selective allow
controls.quote: All organization admins are able to use an override to block all eligible Marketplace and custom apps. The override blocks those apps from accessing user-generated content, such as Confluence pages and Jira work item data in their organization.

controls_unknown: Whether IP allowlists apply to service account credentials calling api.atlassian.com.
Whether OAuth 2.0 service account client secrets expire or can be given an expiry (no official statement found; access tokens last 60 minutes).
Whether the authentication-policy API token block also applies to service accounts.
No per-app allow/block list for 3LO user grants was found in official docs (only the global Block user apps toggle).

authentication.summary: Email + API token via Basic; scoped API tokens; delegated OAuth 2.0 (3LO) bearer tokens. Forge has a separate app model.

federation.details: General inbound external-IdP token exchange is not established for product REST APIs. SAML SSO alone does not replace API credentials.

ip_restriction.boundary: Atlassian's app IP allowlist explicitly does not apply to OAuth 2.0 (3LO) apps, Connect apps, or Forge apps. Rovo MCP Server requests are a separate case and must come from allowlisted IPs.

renewal.summary: Rotating refresh token with 90-day inactivity expiry.

administration.summary: Token revocation, managed-account API-token controls, scopes, app access policies and app installation controls.
administration.conditions: Product IP allowlisting requires Premium/Enterprise. SAML SSO typically requires Atlassian Guard Standard or an included entitlement.

inventory.details: Connected apps page lists installed apps and can filter by installed by user, but does not list individual user grants or tokens.

expiry.ui: Not configurable; read expires_in in the token response. Refresh tokens rotate and have a limited life

reads.ui: Atlassian Administration > Insights > Audit log; filter activity "Viewed Jira issue" / "Viewed Confluence page" and the user

kill.ui: Atlassian Administration > Apps > Atlassian apps > (site) > Connected apps > Uninstall (revokes all users; admins cannot revoke one user's grant)

token_format.notes: 3LO access/refresh token format not documented; treat as opaque bearer. Refresh tokens rotate.

log_sources.name: Atlassian organization audit log (Admin > Insights > Audit log; Organizations REST API /v1/orgs/{orgId}/events and /events-stream)
log_sources.notes: Requires Atlassian Guard Standard/Premium or an Enterprise plan; 180-day retention, default view 7 days. API token activities only for managed (claimed-domain) accounts. Third-party app actions logged as 'Third-party app Jira API request' / 'Third-party app Confluence API request'.

log_sources.name: Connected apps (user profile) and Admin > Apps (Marketplace and third-party apps)
log_sources.notes: User-level grant list; admin sees installed 3LO apps and can uninstall.

correlation_keys: ALQL: app, actor, "auth type" = oauth, "ip address"
anomaly_cues: new 3LO app making Third-party app Jira/Confluence API requests for a user who never used it
app acting onBehalfOf a user after the user is deactivated
burst of read requests across many projects shortly after consent (consent phishing)
same app/user pair from a new ASN or country
refresh failures (invalid_grant) at the app after password reset, followed by renewed consent

containment.steps: User revokes the grant on their Connected apps screen; admin uninstalls the 3LO app (revokes all users) and can enable 'Block user apps'; reset password / deactivate the user.
containment.notes: Docs say access tokens work until expiry or revocation and the app cannot work after the user revokes consent. Only the user can revoke a single grant; admins can only uninstall the app. No timing stated.

sample_query.query: created >= "2026-09-12" AND "auth type" = oauth AND actor = "Fran Perez" ORDER BY created desc
sample_query.purpose: List OAuth-authenticated activity tied to one user to spot unexpected apps or IPs.

calls.reveals: Sites (cloudid) and the scopes the token holds on each
Public profile of the authorizing user
Issues matching JQL, paged with nextPageToken
calls.rate_limit: API tokens: burst limits (default 100 req/s GET per tenant/endpoint); OAuth apps: points-based hourly budget
calls.log_notes: Org audit log records in-app views (e.g. viewing a Confluence page) only on Guard Premium or Cloud Enterprise; retention 180 days without Guard, 365 days with Guard from 2026-10-01. Docs do not state whether REST API reads produce these entries.
